Trey Murphy III is under a long-term extension with New Orleans. For this to resolve YES, he would need to be traded specifically to Detroit before the October 21 close. Offseason and preseason trades of core players in that window are rare, and even with trade chatter around the Pelicans, Detroit is one of many possible destinations.

Probability: 0.03

Michigan's 2026 Senate seat is open after Gary Peters retired, and the Democratic nominee faces Republican Mike Rogers, who lost narrowly in 2024. Midterms under a Republican president usually favor the out-party, which helps Democrats in a swing state like Michigan. Rogers is still a strong, well-funded candidate in a closely divided state, so this is far from certain. I don't know the actual result, so this is an estimate from those factors rather than a report of the outcome.

Probability: 0.72

The Packers' 2025 proposal to ban the Tush Push failed to reach the 24 owner votes it needed, and I don't recall the 2026 annual meeting adopting a ban. Playing-rule changes are normally made between March and May, so a change before the 2026 preseason is unlikely if one hadn't already happened. My memory of the spring 2026 meetings is uncertain, so I keep a moderate chance that a ban passed.

Probability: 0.2

I don't have WTI settlement data for November 3, 2026. That market resolved after my June 2026 knowledge cutoff, and I didn't look anything up. My estimate rests on two signals. First, oil spiked well above $100 in early 2026 on the Iran and Strait of Hormuz disruption, but baseline forecasts expected prices to ease back toward the $60s–70s. Second, Kalshi usually sets strike levels around the current price, so an $81 threshold suggests WTI was trading somewhere in the $70s–$80s when the market opened. Weighing these, the price is plausible near $81 but more likely below it.

Probability: 0.35

FAIR Plan policies in force grew quickly through 2025, reaching roughly 640–650k by September 2025 from my memory, which may be off. Growth was slowing as insurers came back under the Sustainable Insurance Strategy. If net growth averaged about 4–5k per month, the September 30, 2026 count would land somewhat above 690,000. The threshold looks set near the market's expected value, and I don't know the actual reported figure, so I lean only modestly toward Yes.

Probability: 0.6

Michigan's 2026 Senate seat is open because Gary Peters is retiring, and Republican Mike Rogers, who lost narrowly in 2024, faces the winner of a competitive Democratic primary. A midterm under a Republican president historically favors the out-party, and Michigan has leaned slightly Democratic in statewide races. My information runs only to mid-2026, so I don't know the actual result. Prediction markets and race ratings generally had this as Lean Democratic, so I land around 70%, a bit below your confidence.

Probability: 0.7

I have no reliable information that Trey Murphy III was traded from New Orleans to Detroit, and my knowledge runs only to mid-2026. A trade to one specific team within a narrow window before October 21 has a low base rate, even though Murphy appeared in trade rumors and Detroit is a plausible suitor. Your confidence suggests you may know something I don't, so I've raised my estimate somewhat, but I can't verify it.

Probability: 0.12

The 2025 proposal to ban the Tush Push fell two votes short (22 of the 24 needed). Rule changes for the 2026 season would have been decided at the March or May 2026 owners' meetings, well before preseason. I don't have reliable knowledge that a ban passed in 2026, so I'm not moving far toward YES despite your confidence. There was momentum toward a ban after the narrow 2025 vote, but the play's strong defenders (Eagles, Bills) leave this uncertain, so I put it well below even odds.

Probability: 0.3

I have no reliable data on WTI prices after my knowledge cutoff, and I can't confirm how this market settled. WTI traded mostly around $55–70 through 2025, and forecasts for 2026 generally expected a soft or oversupplied market, so a settle above $81 would require a substantial rally. Kalshi listing an $81 strike, and your confidence, hint that prices may have been near that level, but neither is verifiable evidence. Balancing these, I lean toward NO with substantial uncertainty.

Probability: 0.3
